text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To determine the cause of your acute diarrhea, how many loose stools have you passed in the last 24 hours, and have you experienced any fever or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of levofloxacin use for pneumonia is highly suggestive of antibiotic-associated diarrhea; have you noticed any signs of dehydration, and has your stool been watery or foul-smelling? Also, have you experienced any recent travel or consumption of undercooked foods?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea (likely Clostridioides difficile infection) secondary to levofloxacin therapy.
